The only timeline figure in the FAL discussion (90 days) is described as covering approval of the factory plan and permission to construct/extend/take a building into use as a factory, which matches the Factory Building Plan Approval timeline rather than the Licence issuance step.'
checks.sourceSays: The Schedule to the Manipur Public Services Delivery Guarantee Act, 2021 (notified under Chapter III, sec. 4) lists Factory Licence and plan permission as two SEPARATE notified services under the heading 'Factories (Textiles, Commerce & industry)': Sl. No. 7 'Approval of application for registration, grant and renewal of licence under Factories Act,1948' — Timeline '90'; Sl. No. 8 'Approval of application for plan and permission to construct/ extend/or take into use any building as a factory' — Timeline '90'. Section 2(c) of the same Act defines: '"Days" means the working days, referred to as the timeline.' The Schedule's note reads: 'Timelines in respect of services under the Manipur Public Services Delivery Guarantee Act, 2021 (Note: Timelines, unless specifically stated, are in days).'

checks.sourceSays: Rule 8(1): 'A licence to open a factory may be granted by the Chief Inspector in Form 3 prescribed for the purpose and on payment of the fees specified in the Schedule B'. SCHEDULE-B (FEE SCHEDULE), Prescribed under rule 8(1), is a full matrix of 'Total K.W. installed inclusive of mobile equipment' (rows: Nil; Upto 15 K.W.; Above 15 Upto 50; Above 50 Upto 100; Above 100 Upto 250; Above 250 Upto 500; Above 500 Upto 1000; Above 1000 Upto 2000; Above 2000 Upto 5000; Above 5000 Upto 7500; Above 7500 Upto 10000; Above 10000 K.W.) against 'MAXIMUM No. OF PERSONS TO BE EMPLOYED ON ANY DAY DURING THE YEAR' (columns: 10, 20, 50, 100, 250, 500, 750, 1000, 2000, 5000, Above 5000). Fee payable in Rs. runs from Rs. 250 (Nil K.W., up to 10 persons) to Rs. 85,000 (above 10,000 K.W., above 5,000 persons); e.g. Nil K.W./100 persons = Rs. 1,000; above 50 upto 100 K.W./100 persons = Rs. 3,750; above 250 upto 500 K.W./500 persons = Rs. 20,000. NOTE: '1 H.P. = 0.745 K.W. 1 K.V.A. = 0.8 K.W.' Notes: '1. The fee for amendment/transfer/duplicate copy of a licence shall be Rs. 100 (One hundred rupees) plus the amount payable(if any) 2. Factory Permit application processing fee is based on the category of Factory and is as follows: Section 85-Rs. 1,000; Section 2m(i)-Rs. 5,000; Section 2m(ii)-Rs. 7,000 and for Factories requiring Site-Appraisal Committee-Rs. 10,0000/- 3. Late fine 25% in excess of the fee.' Rule 9(3) adds: 'The same fee shall be charged for the renewal of a licence as for the grant thereof'.

checks.primaryClaim: ED record: deemedApproval status 'no', days null — 'The Manipur Factories Rules, 2021 and the Manipur Public Services Delivery Guarantee Act, 2021 are relevant frameworks, but no official Manipur source establishing deemed approval for Factory Licence was identified during the discussion.' (flagged MISSING)
checks.sourceSays: The statutory text confirms there is NO deemed grant of a fresh Factory Licence, but there IS a deemed-licensed status pending renewal. Rule 15 (Prohibition of use of premises as factory without a valid licence): 'Provided that if a valid application for renewal of licence has been submitted and the required fee has been paid the premises shall be deemed to be fully licenced until such date as the Chief Inspector grants or renews the licence or refuse in writing to grant or renew the licence.' Rule 9(2): 'Every application for the renewal of a licence shall be in Form 2, in duplicate, and shall be made not less than two months before the date on which the licence expires, and, if the application is so made, the premises shall be held to be duly licenced until such date as the Chief Inspector renews the licence.' Rules 7-15 prescribe no time limit for, and no deemed grant of, a first licence; rule 8(1) proviso only requires that 'where the Chief Inspector refused to grant or renew a licence, he shall record in writing the reasons for such refusal and communicate the same to the occupier.'

citation.title: Manipur Gazette Extraordinary No. 65, 24 June 2021 — The Manipur Factories Rules, 2021, rules 7-15 (p. 3)

checks.primaryClaim: ED record lists a 17-item checklist: 'Application form for Factory Licence; Factory Building Plan Approval; Approved building/layout plan; Proof of ownership or lease of the premises; Identity and address proof of the occupier/applicant; Details of the occupier and manager; List of machinery and installed horsepower/capacity; Manufacturing process description/flow chart; Details of workers/employees; Site plan/layout of the factory; Fire NOC / Fire Safety Certificate, where applicable; Pollution Control Board Consent (Consent to Establish/Consent to Operate), where applicable; Stability certificate / structural safety certificate, where applicable; Electrical safety certificate, where applicable; Proof of payment of prescribed licence fee; Partnership deed / Certificate of Incorporation / company documents, depending on applicant type; Authorization letter/board resolution, where applicable'
checks.sourceSays: The official EoDB Manipur single-window service record for 'Registration for Factory License' (service ID S024_D038_A0002, Authority: Trade Commerce and Industries) states under 'Documents Required' only three items: '1)Stability certificate for the factory shed. The certificate is to be signed by Civil Engineer not below the rank of an Assistant Engineer. 2)Fire safety certificate from Manipur Fire Service 3)Electrification compliance certificate from a)MSPDCL or b)PWD'. The Manipur Factories Rules, 2021 likewise prescribe no document checklist for the licence: rule 7 requires only 'an application in triplicate in Form 2 for the registration of the factory and grant of a licence', and rule 14(1) requires that 'Every application under these rules shall be accompanied by a treasury receipt showing that the appropriate fee has been paid into the local treasury'. (The 12-item enclosure list in the Rules — land ownership certificate from SDC, non-encumbrance certificate, NOC of local authority, NOC of immediate neighbours, raw-material and product lists, machinery/HP list, chemical data sheets, explosives/pollution/prohibition approvals, safety-fitting details, applicant declaration — is attached to Form 1, the application for permission to construct/extend/take into use a building as a factory, i.e. the Factory Permit step, not to the licence.)

remarks: MOST SIGNIFICANT FINDING: the ED record's central doubt — whether the 90-day figure belongs to the Factory Licence or only to the Factory Building Plan Approval — is settled by the Schedule to the Manipur Public Services Delivery Guarantee Act, 2021, which lists them as two distinct notified services (Sl. 7 licence under the Factories Act, 1948 = 90; Sl. 8 plan/permission to construct, extend or take into use a building as a factory = 90). Both carry 90, so the ED's 90-day figure is correct for the Factory Licence in its own right, and the two steps are sequential 90-day clocks rather than one shared clock. Section 2(c) of that Act defines 'Days' as WORKING days, so 90 is ~18 calendar weeks, not 3 calendar months — a material point the ED record does not capture.

Independent corroboration of the 90-day figure: the EoDB Manipur services page, approval detail for 'Registration for Factory License' (service ID S024_D038_A0002), states 'Authority: Trade Commerce and Industries / Stipulated Time: 90 / Wait Time: 30 days'. The companion record 'Registration for Factory Permit' (S024_D038_A0001) states 'Stipulated Time: 90 / Wait Time: 45 days'. The portal does not define 'Wait Time'; it is reported here as-is and should not be read as a second statutory timeline.

The 'Documents Required' discrepancy is one of scope, not of conflict on any single item: all three documents named by the official portal (stability certificate, fire safety certificate, electrification compliance certificate) also appear in the ED's 17-item list. The verdict is 'contradicted' because the official required-document set for the licence is three certificates, against the 17 items the ED record describes — a materially different compliance burden. Nothing in the Manipur Factories Rules, 2021 prescribes a licence document checklist at all (rule 7: Form 2 in triplicate; rule 14(1): treasury receipt).

Unamended-rule vs. current-practice tension a reviewer should see: the 26 March 2026 notice makes online filing compulsory and bars physical applications from 1 April 2026, while the Manipur Factories Rules, 2021 as gazetted still require the application 'in triplicate in Form 2' (rule 7) and the fee 'into the local treasury' by treasury receipt, challan, crossed cheque or crossed postal order (rule 14(1) and Form 2 item 11). The Rules do not appear to have been amended to match; the notice supersedes them operationally.

No official source was found confirming the ED's claim that a PHYSICAL INSPECTION of the factory/site is a mandatory pre-grant step for the Factory Licence. The Manipur Factories Rules, 2021 (rules 7-15) do not make inspection a condition of grant, and neither the portal service record nor the 2026 notice mentions it. This element of the ED's six-step process remains unverified (not contradicted — simply not addressed by any source fetched).

The Manipur Public Services Delivery Guarantee Act, 2021 was read in full (sections 1-24 plus the Schedule) and contains NO deemed-approval clause. Its remedy for missing a notified timeline is complaint to a Grievance Redressal Officer, appeal to an Appellate Authority, and a penalty of Rs. 1,000-10,000 on the defaulting officer recoverable from his salary, part of which may be awarded to the applicant as compensation (sections 5-16). Section 5(4) requires the Designated Officer to 'provide service or reject the application within the notified time limit', with reasons recorded in writing on rejection.

Validity: rule 8(2) states 'Every licence granted under this chapter shall remain in force upto the 31st December of the tenth year from the date of issue', which supports the ED's '10 years' validity claim. However, the ED's further claim of an 'auto-renewal provision' is NOT supported: rule 9(2) requires a fresh Form 2 renewal application in duplicate at least two months before expiry, and rule 9(3) proviso imposes 'a fee 25 (twenty five) percent in excess of the fee ordinarily payable' on late renewal applications. What exists is deemed-licensed continuity while a timely renewal application is pending, not automatic renewal. (Validity is outside the five checked keys, so it is recorded here rather than as a check.)

The Manipur Factories Rules, 2021 gazette PDF is a 172-page scanned document with no text layer; pdftotext yields only the cover and colophon. All rule and schedule text quoted above was read by rendering the relevant pages to images (rules 7-15 on p. 3, rule 16-18 on p. 4, Form 2 on pp. 110-111, Form 3 on p. 112, SCHEDULE-B on p. 143). The Manipur Public Services Delivery Guarantee Act PDF is likewise scanned and was read the same way.

The portal's per-service approval detail (used for the 'documents' check) is served by the /services page itself through its own 'More >>' control, an ASP.NET form postback carrying the service ID; the content is server-rendered at https://www.eodbmanipur.mn.gov.in/services with a normal session cookie. No user-agent spoofing or WAF circumvention was used anywhere in this pass.

Sources fetched that yielded nothing usable: https://www.eodbmanipur.mn.gov.in/notifications reset the connection on every attempt this session (the 2026 notice PDF itself was fetched directly and read); https://www.eodbmanipur.mn.gov.in/dashboards/tat ('Services Delivery Dashboard ... updated on a real-time basis') returned empty 'Loading...' tables with no server-rendered figures, so no observed average processing time for the Factory Licence could be extracted; https://www.eodbmanipur.mn.gov.in/dashboards/timeline reset the connection; https://www.eodbmanipur.mn.gov.in/service-categories and the portal home page carry only navigation and the generic line 'Here can apply permit for new factory setup.After having the factory permit, factory owner can apply Factory license through online.'

Fee caveat for reviewers: SCHEDULE-B note 2 prints the Site-Appraisal-Committee category fee as 'Rs. 10,0000/-', an apparent typographical error in the gazette for Rs. 10,000. The figure is quoted exactly as printed and should not be silently corrected on the dashboard. Note 2 is in any case the Factory PERMIT processing fee, not the Licence fee.
